notes.title: TRF will become free soon.
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

As a quick update, I just wanted to say that TRF will become Free to Play soon. I enjoyed working on this game, but other things have taken priority in my life, and I can no longer support this project I began as a hobby.

Because of TRF reaching end of support, I decided to switch the game to Free To Play on all platforms, Steam, Xbox and Android. This will occur over the coming days.

Thanks to everyone who bought and enjoyed the game over the past few years, it's been fun!

Kind Regards,
Oliver

notes.title: TRF is out now and Free-To-Play on Android devices!
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

Just a quick post to let you know that TRF is now available for Android over on the Google Play Store.

The game is fairly similar to the PC release, however has a few omissions, due to the nature of mobile devices.

The game is singleplayer
There is currently no track creator, although a simplified version may be added.
There is no ability to share tracks.
There is no Elimination mode.

Other than that, the core gameplay is intact. And there is time trial mode with leaderboards.

You can download it over at: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.oliverstogden.trf

I hope you all enjoy!

notes.title: Version 2021-018 Released! Fuel/Tyre Wear, 2 new tracks based on Real Locations!
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

This update has been a little while in the works, and in preparation for the Career mode that I'm working on for TRF, I've added Tyre Wear and Fuel to the game.

These are both somewhat experimental features, to use them you need to enable "Fuel/Tyre Wear" as a mutator for your event. It only works in the 'Race' game mode, and it only works on tracks which have at least 8 pit buildings placed in them.

If you are making tracks, make sure the pit stops are close to the track, and easily accessible, as the AI basically need to be near a pit and have a straight line to the pit in order to use them.

2 new tracks have also been added to the game, which have support for pit stops, they are based in Britain and Australia, specifically on Silverstone and Albert Park.

There is also a bunch of bug fixes which has fixed some new as well as longstanding issues, here's the full patch notes:

2021-018 (30-11-2021):

ADD: Added Real World Location Track: Australia
ADD: Added Real World Location Track: Britain
ADD: Added Fuel usage to cars. (Activated by a Mutator)
ADD: Added Tyre wear to cars. (Activated by a Mutator)
ADD: Pit stop buildings can now be used to refuel and replace tyres. 8 Pit stops must be on the track to work.
NOTE: Pit Stops must be placed on/near the track to work, as the AI need a clear path to drive to them from the racing line.

FIX: Fix an issue where terrain was incorrectly placed when loading up a track in the editor.
FIX: Finally fixed the pit-stop building collision issues.
FIX: Fixed no maps being available for Kill Trail mode.
FIX: Fixed some terrain detection issues where terrain was misplaced by 2000 pixels to the North West.
FIX: Fixed AI not being slowed down by being on a poor terrain type.
FIX: Terrain is now visible again on the main menu.
FIX: Gamepads will no longer vibrate for no reason when the car is stationary.
FIX: Fixed the wrong part of the track being visually "underwater" in both the game and track previews.
FIX: Fixed some terrain decals being incorrectly placed on water.

Thanks for your support!

- Oliver

To celebrate, a new update is being released, this update adds a new game mode that is playable by up to 4 players.

It is based on the TRON/Snake, where each car leaves a trail behind it, and has to try and make the other drivers hit their trail, whilst not slowing down themselves, or hitting another trail, including their own!

Alongside this, dynamic rain and dynamic snow are appearing as new weather types, when the weather is set to these, the intensity of rain/snow will vary throughout the race, causing changing driving conditions and visibility.

I hope you all enjoy this update, here's the full changelog:

CHANGE: Some default settings changed, zoom level changed from 1.25 to 1.5, and the track map is now on by default.

notes.content:
Hello everyone!

I've been working really hard over April and into May to bring you this latest update to TRF, with the longest changelog yet!

The major changes are:

Cops & Racers game mode added.
5 New Tracks added.
Extra objects to place in the editor.
Gamepad support in the Track Editor
32-bit Support Removed, the game now requires a 64-bit OS.
Online play has been removed.
A ton of bug fixes.

The removal of online play was a sad moment for me, but the content I was able to add because of its removal was worth it in my opinion, and I think the majority of the players will benefit from it.

Here are the full patch notes for this release:

2021-013 (11-05-2021):

From this point onwards TRF requires a 64-bit OS. 32-bit may be able to continue to be unofficially supported on another branch, but you should not purchase the game unless you use a 64-bit OS.

ADD: Gamepad support added for the track editor.

ADD: Experimental support for spawning cars near where the previous round ended on Advanced tracks in Elimination mode. Previously you always started from the start/finish line in Elimination mode on Advanced tracks.

CHANGE: The base game engine has been updated.
CHANGE: Executable is now a 64-bit exe, not 32-bit, this brings a big improvement to performance.
CHANGE: When using Up/Down or LB/RB to change selected object in the track editor, the page will keep up with the selected objects page.

notes.title: Removal of Online Multiplayer and the future of TRF
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

This isn't a decision I've made lightly, or one I'm particularly pleased to make, but I feel it's for the best.

I've been keeping an eye on the statistics for online play, and it seems like it's only been used a handful of times since the game launched, and on top of that, the time it takes for me to make every game mode, every slight change in gameplay, work in the network part of the game is very time consuming as someone working alone.

Given that hardly anyone plays TRF online, and it almost doubles my workload to support the online mode, the next major patch to TRF will remove online multiplayer from the game.

If you have a good internet connection, you could use Steam's Remote Play Together feature to stream your game to friends and let them play the local multiplayer mode with you. Or use another service such as Parsec.

What are the benefits to this change?

Mainly that I will be able to release content more frequently and faster. I don't have to run checks and multiplayer tests, which are hard to do for a solo dev, and take up a significant amount of time.

Also, content that has until now been held back due to not working in the games network mode, can now be freely released. This includes a new game mode, which is almost ready.

The store page has been updated to remove any mention of online multiplayer, so any new purchases are not under the assumption that the online mode will stay in the game.

As I'm not a network programmer, your experience with Remote Play Together or Parsec may be smoother than playing online anyway. :)

Thank you for all your support,
Oliver

notes.title: New Track Editor Released!
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

It's been a month since the last update, but I've been working for hours each day to bring you this new feature!

The track editor is getting a new "advanced" mode. In this mode, you can place "nodes" to define the track shape, rather than placing pre-defined track pieces. The new mode also lets you modify the terrain, allowing you to add water to your tracks, without making them entirely water.

The old editor remains, and is now listed as the "basic" editor when you open the track creator.

Here's a quick timelapse of me making a simple track in the new "advanced" editor:
[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/YWUpjZ8R4dxlN6Hjc0/giphy.gif[/img]

This will hopefully allow the creation of new and interesting tracks, definitely it will allow you to make tracks that closely represent what tracks would in real life.

[img]https://i.ibb.co/CHJmzWP/Terrain-Editor-4.png[/img]

There are still some things I would like to add and refine with the editor, so stay-tuned for future updates to it.

That's not all that's been added in this months update however. A new mutator has been added, which can be purchased for 5,000 coins in the in-game shop. A few people wanted a more "realistic" experience with the cars, and for them to be less drifty. I don't know if I achieved what they wanted with this, but I had fun making it!

The mutator will basically add weight to the cars, make them accelerate/decelerate slower, and make them turn slower. It means you may need to start braking to handle the corners properly when you have it enabled. The AI have been modified to take the extra weight of the cars into account, but they might still have some oddities while I work this out.

And with the 2 main features of this update out of the way, here's the full patch notes for your enjoyment!

2021-010 (29-03-2021):

ADD: Added the ability to create tracks using splines.
ADD: Added the ability to alter terrain in the track editor.
ADD: Added a choice of which editor and environment you want to use when first making a track/arena.
ADD: Added "Settings Applied" text when saving and applying settings in the options menu, so players have confirmation their settings are saved.
ADD: Readded Delete Progress and Delete Ghost Data buttons back into the options menu.
ADD: Added a new mutator "Sim-ish Racing".

CHANGE: Terrain graphics for the environments have changed.
CHANGE: Environments in the track editor are now set when you first make a track, and cannot be changed afterwards.
CHANGE: Fonts have been changed slightly.
CHANGE: Updated the auto-generate scenery button to generate scenery a little more randomly and varied.
CHANGE: AI scores generated for Zen mode have been lowered slightly.
CHANGE: Boats are now faster in Zen mode.

FIX: Fixed the Reset text being off-screen for P1.
FIX: Fixed the cursor in the track editor being below certain buttons.
FIX: Fixed a crash when loading tracks with nothing in them, particularly occured when loading autosaves.
FIX: You should now be able to download Steam Workshop tracks/arenas with the gamepad in-game.
FIX: You can finish in Time Trial mode again.
FIX: The track map is now aligned properly in Time Trial mode again.
FIX: Fixed some issues with map previews for workshop items.
FIX: You can now browse more than 10 tracks/arenas in the download tracks menu.
FIX: You can no longer place more than 8 spawn points in a battle arena, as doing so resulted in a crash.
FIX: Arena spawn points weren't clickable to place if you weren't on page 1 for objects, this has been fixed.
FIX: Fixed an issue where all cars would be considered to have a turbo.
FIX: Fixed various sound issues with Zen mode.
FIX: Fixed an issue where you couldn't complete more than 1 lap in Zen mode on tracks with a crossroad.
FIX: Fixed the arrow keys rotating objects incorrectly in the track editor.

REMOVE: Removed 2 objects from the track editor that should not have been placeable.

As always, please report any bugs you find and any suggestions you have either in the forums here on Steam, or over on the TRF Discord server at: https://bit.ly/2OIgGPq

Thank you all so much for your support, TRF has had more support the past 2 weeks than it has since launch, and I'm grateful for that.

- Oliver

notes.title: TRF is 40% off in the Steam Remote Play Together Sale!
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

Pleased to announce that TRF is 40% off for the next few days as part of the Steam Remote Play Together sale.

Remote Play Together is a handy built-in feature of Steam, which lets you play split-screen games over the internet by streaming your screen to your friends. They can play with you using their controller, as if they were at your PC with you!

TRF supports Remote Play Together to let friends enjoy the frantic 4 player split-screen action!

On top of that, the new track editor, which features terrain editing and an improved way to build tracks, has entered public beta, you can try it out by switching to the 'neweditor' branch in your game properties.

notes.title: POLL: Should TRF get a "driving style" option?
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

Currently the vehicles in TRF are quite drifty, except for Kart and Formula classes.

As this is quite a divisive driving style, I was wondering what people thought about me adding an option to choose driving style in custom races. So you could toggle between drifting and grippy cars.

Some things to note:

1. In network races, the driving style would be determined by the host.
2. In Time Trial mode, drifting driving style would remain, otherwise all times until now would need to be reset.

With that out of the way, here's the poll to vote in, I'm hosting this poll in a few places, so this poll alone won't determine the outcome, but I would be interested to see if a driving style option has any support: https://strawpoll.com/1dcvwcpz2

Thanks everyone for reading.

notes.title: The Race Factory - Developer Livestream
notes.content:
We'll spend a couple of hours looking at the game, playing some of the game modes, setting some times on the online leaderboards, and creating a basic race track in the editor.

Come hang out and chat at 3PM BST on Sunday the 11th of October!

TRF is a multiplayer top-down racing game, with a variety of game modes, vehicles, and a track editor included with the game. Inspired largely by racing titles of the 80's and 90's, TRF hopes to capture the feel of these classics, while offering modern features such as online multiplayer and leaderboards.

notes.title: Welcome to The Race Factory!
notes.content:
Thank you for checking out The Race Factory!

My name is Oliver, and this has been my project for the past 2 years.

It is a top-down racing game, inspired by classic racing games that I grew up with from the 80's on 90's on Commodore/Atari systems and the SNES/PS1.

The game features a variety of vehicles, from regular cars, to Formula vehicles, Trucks and Boats. It also features several game modes, all of which are playable by up to 4 players locally and up to 8 players online. There is also a track editor included in the game.

Most cars are designed to be drifted, however Formula cars and Karts stick to the road and require quick reactions.

Here are the features in the Steam Games Festival Demo:

[list]
[*]7 Tracks
[*]4 Vehicles Classes: Street, Sports, Super, Formula
[*]1 Battle Arena
[*]4 Game Modes: Race, Elimination, Drift, Infection
[*]1-4 Player Local Multiplayer
[*]Track Editor, however playing user-made tracks is unavailable
[*]Street Car Championship
[/list]

I hope you enjoy playing the games demo, if you enjoy what you play, then it would be great if you could wishlist the game ready for its release later this year.

I will be livestreaming the game on Monday 12th of October, at 3PM BST / 10AM EST / 7AM PST. Feel free to pop-by and hang out in chat!

Thank you for reading, and playing!

- Oliver Stogden

notes.title: What's been happening since the Steam Games Festival? Online play is coming!
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

Just a quick update on a few things as I don't post much on Steam News, I mostly use Twitter.

The Steam Games Festival went quite well for TRF, almost doubling the amount of wishlists the game had. And generating several thousand views to the store page.

The game had been due to release at the end of the Games Festival, at the end of June. However I ran into some issues with the 8 player controller setup for local play. Unfortunately, in order to comply with Steam regulations, I've had to lower the amount of supported local players from 8 to 4. This was a real shame to me, as I wanted to make sure the game could be played by as many people as possible in as many scenarios as possible.

To that end, I decided to delay the release of the game to September, and use the time that gave me to add online multiplayer to TRF.

I've spent the past 4 weeks working exclusively on adding online/LAN multiplayer to the game, if you follow me on my [url=https://twitter.com/O_Stogden]Twitter[/url], you'll have seen frequent updates, including GIFs, to show how the network multiplayer is progressing.

Right now, I have 3/9 game modes working in network play (Time Trial currently isn't planned to support network play). Those game modes are Race, Drift & Zen. The current focus is the Elimination game mode, which is similar to how classic Micro Machines plays.

So that's basically what I've been up to the past month, polishing parts of the game off, and mostly adding the ability to play over a network.

Thanks for reading,
Oliver

notes.title: Time Trial mode & Steam Leaderboard integration
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

The past couple of weeks I've been trying to add some form of competition with other players, as the multiplayer in TRF is local/couch multiplayer only.

My solution to this was to add online leaderboards.

I'm happy to announce that a Time Trial mode has been added to the game, along with in-game Missions, both of these connect to Steam and upload your best times to the games online leaderboards.

Firstly we'll talk about the Mission mode.

These are generally short challenges, taking place in controlled environments (off the race track). Think similar to Gran Turismo's License tests. The first few are simple, and are good for getting used to the games car physics, such as going through a series of cones in a slalom, or a short circuit. Later ones present more challenging driving situations.

Each mission has a Bronze, Silver and Gold medal time, so try and get Gold on every mission!

And now we come to the Time Trial Mode:

In Time Trials, you are forced to drive in certain conditions. Firstly, you are put into a Super class car. The weather and time of day is always clear and midday. You will have to complete 3 laps of the track.

Time Trial mode is currently available for the base tracks that will be included when the game launches in June 2020. I will look into if I can add leaderboard support for user-made tracks, however I believe this might be a difficult ask, so for now, I can only confirm that the base tracks included with the game will support this mode.

The game will launch with 12 base tracks, however I plan to release further tracks after the games release.

A shield power-up has also been added, as my private testers felt it would be nice to have a way of defending yourself instead of being at the mercy of weapons.

The game entered private beta testing last Friday, the 27th March 2020, and I've been getting very valuable feedback on the game from them.

Thanks for reading!
- Oliver

notes.title: Game Features planned for June Release
notes.content:
Hi Everyone!

Today's post is just a summary of all that the game is planned to have for its launch in June.

Here's what the game is planned to have:

[b]Gamemodes: [/b]

At least 8, currently we have 7:

Race: Simple racing gamemode, finish the set number of laps, features weapons which can be turned on and off. 1-4 Players, played on race tracks.

Elimination: Shared-screen eliminator mode, think Micro-Machines, falling off the screen is death. Last car standing wins a point, first to set number of points wins. 1-8 Players, played on race tracks.

Drift: A target score is generated for the track, drift around corners and keep your combos on the straights to earn big points, car collisions are disabled. 1-4 Players, played on race tracks.

Zen: A target score is generated for the track, your cars power is constantly increasing, your car is always accelerating and there are no brakes, you earn points when driving around the track, but if you fall off the track, your points stop increasing. The driver who stays on the track the most when time runs out is the winner here! 1-4 Players, played on race tracks.

Infection: 1 Player starts as infected, their aim is to infect all the other cars by touching them. If a player becomes infected, they then have to infect other cars to earn points. Try to stay alive until the timer runs out to win in this game mode! 1-8 Players, played on battle arenas.

Pass The Bomb: A bomb is randomly placed on a car, they have to touch someone to pass it to them, if you have the bomb when the fuse runs out, BOOM, you're out of the event. Surviving as long as possible is how you earn points here. 1-8 Players, played on battle arenas.

Hold The Gold: A gold bar is placed somewhere on the map, race to pick it up, and then hold onto it for as long as you can! Being hit by another car will transfer the gold to them, whoever holds the gold earns points. Holding the gold for the most amount of time when the timer runs out will win you the event! 1-8 Players, played on battle arenas.

[b]Track Editor:[/b]

There will be a fully-functioning track editor in the final game. It's what I've used to make all the tracks currently in the game. It's capable of making both Race Tracks and Battle Arenas. It contains a racing-line editor so you can tune the AI to your standards, as well as determining what classes as "cheating" on your race tracks, stopping people from cutting corners.

[b]4 Car Classes, each with 8 cars to drive:[/b]

There are 4 car classes in the game, Street, Sports, Super & Hyper.

Car performance in each class is identical, however there are 8 styles of car in each class you can choose from. Sports is the default class, and is recommended for most drivers to start with, Hyper is for more advanced drivers who want a challenge.

[b]Controller Support:[/b]

The following controllers have been tested and work with TRF: Xbox 360 Controller, Xbox One Controller, Dualshock 4. Mouse & Keyboard also work.

[b]Local Multiplayer Support:[/b]

All game modes support at least 4 players, and some game modes support up to 8 players. Every game mode also has support for AI Drivers that will fill up the grid. When playing 1-4 player, the screen will be split. 5-8 player games, the screen will be zoomed out so everyone can fit on the screen.

[b]Weather & Time of Day:[/b]

The game has various weather conditions for you to choose from:

Clear, Rain, Stormy, Snow, Blizzard, Meteor.

Adverse weather conditions will affect car performance, so don't expect to stay on the road in a blizzard! And Meteor showers can really switch up a race.

There are also time of day settings to choose from, Dawn, Day, Dusk & Night.

[b]Mutators:[/b]

Along with the standard event settings, such as amount of laps, weather and time of day, there are also extra "Mutators" you can set for an event.

These range from adding the Zen mode "Always Accelerating" feature to any game mode. Or making the road permanently icy, as though you were in a blizzard. You could even turn off the "drafting" feature, if it's annoying you that people keep catching you up in Infection!

This covers most of what the game has.

Have a good day everyone!
